summary: This note describes the wedding dress worn by Princess Elizabeth, later Queen Elizabeth II, at her wedding to Philip Mountbatten, Duke of Edinburgh, on 20 November 1947 in Westminster Abbey. The dress was designed by Norman Hartnell, and the note explains that clothing rationing meant the material had to be bought with ration coupons. It also covers Hartnell's design style and the dress's fabric and features.
one_line: Describes the 1947 wedding dress of Princess Elizabeth, designed by Norman Hartnell and bought with ration coupons.
key_facts: The wedding dress of Princess Elizabeth was worn by the future Queen Elizabeth II at her wedding to Philip Mountbatten, Duke of Edinburgh.
The wedding took place on 20 November 1947 in Westminster Abbey.
Because of clothing rationing at the time, Princess Elizabeth still had to purchase the material for the dress using ration coupons.
The dress was designed by Norman Hartnell.
Norman Hartnell's signature was said to be embroidery.
Norman Hartnell enjoyed "working with soft, floating fabrics, particularly tulle and chiffon, and with plain, lustrous silks".
The dress was made of soft Damascus Prokar.
The dress had a high neckline.
The dress had a tailored bodice.
The dress had a short train.
